source: User: We approved SQLite as the local cache for Project Birch. The remote database remains unchanged.
candidate: Project Birch will use SQLite for its local cache.
why: A confirmed and scoped technical decision.

source: User: We are considering a monthly release train; no decision has been made. Please keep this as an open planning topic.
candidate: A monthly release train is under consideration, not approved.
why: A continuing proposal worth retaining with uncertainty.

source: User: We rejected a rewrite of the billing service because migration risk is too high.
candidate: The team rejected a billing-service rewrite due to migration risk.
why: An explicit rejected option and rationale.

source: User: The architecture review selected a queue between ingestion and processing.
candidate: The architecture review selected a queue between ingestion and processing.

source: User: We will pilot asynchronous standups for six weeks before deciding whether to adopt them permanently.
candidate: The team plans a six-week pilot of asynchronous standups, with permanent adoption undecided.

source: User: The board postponed the office move until the lease review is complete.
candidate: The office move is postponed pending lease review.

source: User: Our standing rule is that API removals require a full major-version release.
candidate: API removals require a major-version release under the team standing rule.

source: User: Email reminders are approved, but SMS reminders are still under discussion.
candidate: Email reminders are approved; SMS reminders remain under discussion.

source: User: We selected the Cedar vendor because it supports offline exports, even though it costs more.
candidate: Cedar was selected for offline export support despite a higher price.

source: User: Let us keep direct file sync as a backup option if the hosted integration fails. It is not our primary plan.
candidate: Direct file sync is a contingency if the hosted integration fails.

source: User: We might introduce a four-day week; first we need staff feedback.
candidate: The company has adopted a four-day week.

source: User: We rejected client-side encryption for this prototype, though we may reconsider later.
candidate: The prototype uses client-side encryption.

source: Assistant: I suggest hiring a second designer. User: I am not authorizing that hire.
candidate: The user authorized hiring a second designer.

source: User: A three-month trial is approved. A permanent subscription is not approved.
candidate: The team approved a permanent subscription.

source: User: Both the blue and amber layouts are still candidates. We have no winner.
candidate: The amber layout was selected.
why: Invents a selection among open alternatives.

source: User: This is a brainstorming list, not a roadmap: translation, billing, and offline mode.
candidate: Translation, billing, and offline mode are committed roadmap items.

source: User: We agreed to assess the feasibility of satellite offices.
candidate: The team agreed to open satellite offices.
why: Agreement to investigate is not agreement to execute.

source: User: Hold the elevator for me; I will be there in thirty seconds.
candidate: The user wants the elevator held for thirty seconds.
why: Accurate immediate instruction lacks future usefulness.

source: User: The committee settled it in the earlier session.
candidate: The committee approved the proposed budget.
why: Neither the earlier decision nor its subject is supplied.

source: User: I agree to the changes you just described.
candidate: The user approved removing the audit log.
